transcript.text:
“Won’t come on” can mean two quite different things. If the clock/display is working, the common free fix is that the timer has gone into AUTO after a power interruption, so the oven is prevented from heating. If everything is dead, it is more likely to be the cooker isolator/supply or house circuit. 1. If there is a clock, look for AUTO/A or a flashing time. Set the clock to the correct time and select the MANUAL/hand symbol, then try an oven function again. This does not need a part.
2. If there are no signs of life at all, check the cooker isolation switch is on and check whether a circuit breaker/RCD has tripped. Do not remove any panels or wiring covers. Is the clock/display lit (possibly flashing or showing AUTO/A), or is the oven completely dead with no display or light?
display is lit and flashing 0.00 with a little symbol. power went off last night. how do i set the clock? no manual

The flashing 0:00 after last night’s power cut is very likely the clock/timer reset, rather than an oven fault. The oven often will not heat until the time is set and the timer is put back into manual mode. Try this with the cooker left powered on: 1. Look for a button with a clock symbol, or a button marked Mode/Timer. Press it once or hold it for 2–5 seconds until the time digits flash.
2. Set the current time using +/–, ▲/▼, or two buttons marked with arrows.
3. Press the clock/Mode button again, or wait a few seconds, to save it.
4. If there is a little hand symbol or a Manual button, press it until the hand shows and any AUTO/A indication disappears. Then select an oven cooking function and temperature. Avoid switching it off at the wall again while doing this, as that will reset the clock back to 0:00. The small symbol may be the automatic-timer symbol, but the exact button sequence varies. Tell me the markings on the buttons around the display and I can guide you through that layout.
ok did that, set the time and it came on and is heating now

That suggests it was the clock/timer reset after the power cut, not an oven fault. Keep the clock set and avoid switching the cooker off at the wall unless necessary, as some ovens return to AUTO and will not heat until the time is set again.

candidates: Cooker power supply, isolator or tripped circuit (medium)
plan: The fault they reported is: "won't come on". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
